translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "al-Qāriʿa." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:

The Striking Calamity (1) What is the Striking Calamity? (2) And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? (3) On the day when people will be like scattered moths (4) and the mountains will be like fluffed wool (5) As for him whose scales are heavy (6) he will be in a pleasant life (7) and as for him whose scales are light (8) his mother will be Hāwiya (9) And what will make you know what it is? (10) A blazing fire (11)
He, exalted be His mention, says:
is the Hour whose terror strikes (
) the hearts of people, together with the great affliction that befalls them then. It will come in a morning after which there is no night.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: : it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God magnified it and warned His servants of it. [Fn 1]

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he said: it is the Hour.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: . He said: it is the Hour.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us.
m: He said: I heard that al-Qāriʿa, al-Wāqiʿa and al-Ḥāqqa are the Resurrection. [Fn 1]

x: . He, exalted be His mention, says this to magnify the matter of the Resurrection and of the Hour whose terror alarms the servants: what thing is al-Qāriʿa? He means: what thing is the Hour whose terror strikes creation? How great it is, how dreadful and how terrifying.
And what will make you know what al-Qāriʿa is?
. He, exalted be His mention, says to His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: what has made you aware, Muḥammad, what thing al-Qāriʿa is?
On the day when people will be like scattered moths
. He, exalted be His mention, says: al-Qāriʿa is on the day when people will be like the
, which is what falls into the fire and the lamp, and is neither a mosquito nor a fly. By
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: On the day when people will be like scattered moths
that you have seen flutter into the fire. [Fn 2]

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: On the day when people will be like scattered moths
, he said: this is a likeness that God drew.

x: Some of the people of Arabic [Fn 3] used to say that the meaning is: like a swarm of locusts, one mounting another. In the same way people on that day will surge, one into another. [Fn 3]
and the mountains will be like fluffed wool
. He, exalted be His mention, says: on the day the mountains will be like carded wool.
is wool in its various colors.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: and the mountains will be like fluffed wool

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.

x: It was mentioned that the mountains will be moved across the earth while still in the form of mountains, but like dust particles.
As for him whose scales are heavy
. He says: as for him whose scales of good deeds are heavy. By
He means weight. The Arabs say: "You have with me a dirham in the
of your dirham and the weight of your dirham." They also say: "My house is in the
of your house and the weight of your house," meaning opposite your house. The poet said [Fn 3]:

lines: Before I met you I was a man of strength;
for every opponent I had his measure (

x: " he means the opponent's speech and what refutes his argument. Mujāhid used to say: there is no scale; it is only a parable that was drawn. Abū Kurayb narrated this to us.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: There is no scale; it is only a parable drawn. [Fn 1]

x: he will be in a pleasant life
. He says: he will be in a life with which he is content in Paradise.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: he will be in a pleasant life

x: And as for him whose scales are light (8) his mother will be Hāwiya
. He says: as for him whose weight of good deeds is light, his refuge and dwelling is al-Hāwiya, in which he plunges headfirst into Hell.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: And as for him whose scales are light (8) his mother will be Hāwiya
: it is the Fire, which is their refuge.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: . He said: his destination is the Fire, which is al-Hāwiya. Qatāda said: it is an Arabic expression. When a man fell into a severe affair, he would say: "His mother has fallen" (

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ashʿath b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Aʿmā.
m: He said: When a believer dies, his spirit is taken to the spirits of the believers, and they say: "Give rest to your brother, for he was in the distress of the world." He said: They ask him, "What did so-and-so do?" He says: "He died. Did he not come to you?" They say: "They took him to his mother, al-Hāwiya." [Fn 1]

c: Ismāʿīl b. Sayf al-ʿIjlī told me, he said: ʿAlī b. Mushir told us, he said: Ismāʿīl told us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ.
m: , he said: they plunge into the Fire on their heads. [Fn 2]

c: Ibn Sayf told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Sawwār told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatāda.
m: . He said: he plunges into the Fire headfirst. [Fn 3]

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: , he said: al-Hāwiya is the Fire. It is his mother and his refuge, to which he returns and in which he finds shelter. And he recited:
and their refuge is the Fire

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: : this is a parable for it. He made the Fire his mother only because it became his refuge, as a woman gives shelter [Fn 5] to her son. Since he had no refuge other than it [for him] [Fn 6], He made it stand to him in the position of a mother.

x: And what will make you know what it is? (10)
. He, glorified be His mention, says to His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: what has made you aware, Muḥammad, what al-Hāwiya is? Then He explained what it is, saying: it is
) He means a fire that has become hot from the fuel upon it.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to the author and ʿAbd ibn Humayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: This is al-Farraʾ, in Maʿani al-Qurʾan (3/286).
ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/392) from Maʿmar with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 392 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: The verse is cited in al-Farraʾ’s Maʿani al-Qurʾan (3/287).
See the earlier discussion at 10/68 and 16/286.
Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to the author and ʿAbd ibn Humayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/392) from Maʿmar with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 392 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/490) from the author. ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/392) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 490 عن المصنف، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 392 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/490), and al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/385) to the author.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 490، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 385 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Manuscripts T1, T2, and T3 read “taʾwi.”
